exceptions.warning: RECURRING MONTHLY CONVENTION: the agreement states interest as a flat 'annual rate / 12' on the beginning balance -- a day-count-INDEPENDENT monthly-equivalent, not a real actual/360 or actual/365 day count. Verified against the borrower's own Debt Service tab: 2025-02 (28 days) Cash Interest $921,522.81 = beginning debt x 0.1064/12 exactly; 2025-03 (31 days) Cash Interest $919,679.76 = beginning debt x 0.1064/12 exactly -- the SAME per-dollar monthly rate applies regardless of the number of calendar days in the month. This is closer to a 30/360 bond-basis monthly-equivalent than to either convention debt_service.py v1 supports (actual/360 or actual/365 with REAL calendar-day counting; there is no flat/30-360 mode). 'actual/365' is recorded here because it is the closer of the two on an ANNUAL basis: a full non-leap year's real days sum to exactly 365, so actual/365 totals to exactly the stated annual rate over a full 12-month year with zero aggregate drift, whereas actual/360 systematically overcounts annual interest by 365/360 (~1.39%) every year, compounding to a materially overstated total interest figure over the facility's 5-year life. Expect the GENERATED schedule's month-by-month cash-interest figures to differ from the borrower's own booked Debt Service tab in every ordinary month (higher in 31-day months, lower in 28-day February), even though the annual total should be close.

FUNDING-MONTH STUB (January 2025), MATERIAL: the agreement states a mid-month effective/closing date (2025-01-15) and separately states 'January accrual is allocated between legacy and successor debt without duplicate interest' -- implying THIS facility's own share of January's interest is prorated for the ~17 days it existed after closing. The borrower's OWN books instead record a FULL month of both cash interest ($923,369.55) and scheduled principal ($208,278.85) against this facility for January 2025 (Debt Service tab, period 2025-01), consistent with the borrower's Accounting Notes stating explicitly: 'Full-month fee convention: Jan 2025-Dec 2029; final rounding true-up before Jan 15, 2030 maturity' -- i.e. the borrower defers ALL proration to the final stub month at maturity rather than prorating the funding month. debt_service.py v1 always computes a REAL stub from the literal funding date forward (17 of 31 days counted both endpoints in January 2025) and a real stub to the literal maturity date in the final month -- it has no 'full month from inception, true-up entirely at the back end' mode. This spec records the funding date as the agreement's own literally stated date (2025-01-15), NOT backdated to 2025-01-01 to force a match with the borrower's booking convention -- extracting the contract, not the ledger, per Method step 3b. EXPECT the generated schedule's January 2025 cash-interest to run roughly 44% below the borrower's booked full-month figure, and its scheduled-principal to be $0 (this spec's amortization start_date is 2025-02-01) versus the borrower's booked $208,278.85 for that month. Sign-off question: accept this one-time, quantified first-month shortfall as a known engine-limitation gap (the same class of gap as the declining-balance amortization-base issue above), or source month-1 (and eventually the final stub month at maturity) covenant-support figures directly from the borrower's own native Debt Service tab instead.
